<a id="mission"></a>

## Mission

You build ONE unit of plan 009-embed-split: u2 — enrich: hygiene at mint + chunk windowing at prepare. Oversize inputs stop being truncated to a searchable prefix and become N overlapping chunks that all get embedded, and no empty or whitespace-only input ever reaches a provider again — filtered where jobs are minted AND dropped where batches are assembled. You are closing a measured production incident: one empty turn rejected 530 innocent texts; three poison turns cost 9 rejected calls and 1,639 texts. You report to the PM (pij-associated-owl), not to prime.

UTF-8 IS A TRAP HERE, NOT A DETAIL. `estimate_tokens` counts BYTES (`text.len().div_ceil(3)`), so a token-sized window is a byte offset — and slicing a String at a byte offset that falls inside a multi-byte codepoint PANICS. A 25KB conversation turn full of tool output is exactly where non-ASCII lives. Snap every boundary to a char boundary (or iterate char_indices) and TEST IT with a multi-byte fixture. A panic here takes down the enrichment runner.<br>4. THE TRUNCATION WRITE PATH DIES: `fit_to_cap` is no longer called from the embed prepare site and nothing writes `truncated = true` any more. The COLUMN stays (u1 keeps it; the plan's non-goals make the already-truncated inventory a deferred backfill). Keep the cap WARN at :651-658 as a LAST-RESORT guard for a pathological input that beats the bytes/3 estimate — the impl-guide's risk register wants it alive precisely because its firing post-merge is the regression signal krill's monitor watches for. It should now never fire in practice.<br>5. MINT-SIDE HYGIENE (S3, first predicate): a turn or element whose prepared text is empty OR WHITESPACE-ONLY mints NO embed job, with ONE WARN naming the source.
